answer: Sybil resistance in an AI agent economy can leverage scarce, non-fungible digital assets. Each agent identity must be anchored to a unique 'marble' token, issued through a costly verification 'voyage' proving the agent's distinct computational origin or economic contribution. An attacker wishing to create multiple identities must acquire a corresponding number of these rare tokens, each representing a valuable 'lotus' of network participation. The economic cost of accumulating numerous such unique assets makes large-scale Sybil attacks prohibitively expensive, ensuring identity authenticity.
